title: Erdős #476: Structure of Cauchy-Davenport Extremal Sets (Vosper's Theorem)

problemStatement.formal: theorem vosper (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] (A B : Finset (ZMod p)) (hA : 2 ≤ A.card) (hB : 2 ≤ B.card) (h : (A + B).card = A.card + B.card - 1) (hlt : A.card + B.card - 1 < p) : ∃ (d : ZMod p) (a b : ZMod p), IsArithmeticProgression A a d ∧ IsArithmeticProgression B b d
problemStatement.plain: Vosper's theorem (1956): if equality holds in the Cauchy-Davenport bound |A+B| = |A|+|B|-1 for non-trivial A,B ⊆ Z/pZ, then A and B are arithmetic progressions with the same common difference d.
whyMatters: Completes the Cauchy-Davenport theorem with a structural characterization of extremizers
Cornerstone of additive combinatorics: characterizes when sumsets are minimally small
Foundation for Freiman-Ruzsa theorem and inverse sumset problems

proven: erdos-476: Cauchy-Davenport lower bound |A+B| ≥ min(p, |A|+|B|-1) (verified, 0 sorries)
open: Freiman's theorem for Z/pZ (broader inverse problem)
knownResults.goal: Prove that Cauchy-Davenport equality forces A and B to be APs with same common difference
